newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain strike Wednesday shouldn't hit air traffic.
newsitem.headline: Spain strike Wednesday shouldn't hit air traffic.

text.p: A strike planned for Wednesday by Spanish civil servants should not have much impact on air transport to and from Spain, the airports authority AENA said on Tuesday.
The government has imposed near normal staffing levels as the minimums that should be maintained for air traffic controllers, firemen and other airside workers, it said.
"We expect airports to operate as normal, assuming unions repect the minimum staffing levels," an AENA spokeswoman said.
Union spokesmen were not available to comment on their plans. In past strikes minimum staffing levels have generally been observed.
Representatives of Spain's two million civil servants have called a nationwide one day strike to protest at the government's decision to freeze their pay next year.
The government has so far refused to back down.

State-owned companies like Iberia and its subsidiary Aviaco are excluded as they have their own collective agreements on pay. Iberia's passenger and cargo handling services are therefore also excluded.

The state railway company RENFE has called a series of partial strikes of its own between December 16 and 20 to protest the government's creation of a new management company for railways, which workers fear is a first step towards privatisation.
